title: Exploring Forces
seo_title: Exploring Forces Class 8 Science Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Curiosity Chapter 5)
standard_text: Force as a push or a pull; effects of force on motion and shape; contact forces (muscular force, friction) and non-contact forces (gravitational, magnetic, electrostatic); increasing and reducing friction; mass and weight; net force (summary of NCERT Curiosity Chapter 5).
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 8 Science worksheets for NCERT Curiosity Chapter 5: effects of force, contact and non-contact forces, friction and how to change it, gravity, mass and weight, and net force. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A force is a push or a pull.
key_sub: Weight = mass × g; friction opposes motion.
body_html:
How to think about it

A force is a push or a pull measured in newtons. It can start or stop motion, change speed or direction, and change shape. Contact forces need touching (muscular force, friction); non-contact forces act at a distance (gravity, magnetic and electrostatic forces).

Friction opposes motion between surfaces: treads and spikes increase it, while oil, ball bearings and wheels reduce it. Weight is the pull of gravity: weight = mass × g (about 10 N for each kilogram on Earth), and on the Moon it is about one-sixth. Forces in the same direction add; opposite forces subtract.

Example

Weight of a 30 kg child (g = 10)?

W = m × g

Answer: 300 N

Example

Pulls of 400 N and 350 N in opposite directions. Net force?

400 − 350

Answer: 50 N

Common mistakes

  • Confusing mass (kg) with weight (N).
  • Thinking friction always helps motion.
  • Adding forces that act in opposite directions.

faq.q: What is the difference between mass and weight?
faq.a: Mass is the amount of matter (kg) and does not change; weight is the force of gravity on it (N) and changes from place to place.
